html:
About Zhakethketh Group

Zhakethketh Group’s mission is to develop reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We aim for AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and society overall. Our rapidly growing team consists of dedicated researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders collaborating to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

Zhakethketh Group manages one of the largest and fastest-growing accelerator fleets in the industry — covering multiple accelerator families and clouds. The Accelerator Capacity Engineering (ACE) team ensures every chip in that fleet is tracked, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that help Zhakethketh Group plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute.

As an engineer on ACE, you will build the production systems powering this effort: data pipelines that ingest and normalize telemetry from diverse cloud environments, observability tools providing real-time fleet health visibility, and performance instrumentation measuring how efficiently major workloads use hardware. You will write production-quality code daily, operate alongside Kubernetes-native infrastructure at scale, and influence decisions around one of Zhakethketh Group’s largest expenditures.

You’ll work closely with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. This role demands comfort moving between data engineering, systems engineering, and observability, thriving in a high-autonomy, high-ambiguity environment.

What This Team Owns

The team’s responsibilities cover three functional areas. Based on your background and interests, you will primarily focus on one, but these domains overlap and the boundaries are fluid:

 

  • Data infrastructure — collecting, normalizing, and serving fleet-wide data that powers all other work. This involves building pipelines to ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalizing billing and usage data across cloud providers, and maintaining the BigQuery layer used throughout the organization. Correctness, completeness, and latency are critical.

 

  • Fleet observability — making the accelerator fleet’s state understandable and actionable in real time. This includes cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation issues, and driving systemic improvements in scheduling and fragmentation. This work bridges Kubernetes operations and cross-team coordination.

 

  • Compute efficiency — measuring and improving how effectively each major workload utilizes its hardware. This entails instrumenting utilization metrics across training, inference, and evaluation systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, setting per-config baselines, and collaborating with system-owning teams to close efficiency gaps.

 

  • Internal compute tooling — developing platforms and interfaces that make capacity data usable organization-wide. This includes capacity planning tools, workload attribution systems, cost dashboards, and self-service APIs. Users include research engineers, infrastructure teams, finance, and leadership — each with varying technical needs. This work requires product thinking to identify actual user needs, define schema contracts, and enhance data discoverability.

 

You will be assigned to a pod based on your background and interests. We are particularly focused on hiring for the Data Platform pod, but strong candidates for any of the three active pods will be considered.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and operate data pipelines that ingest accelerator occupancy, utilization, and cost data from multiple cloud providers into BigQuery. You will own data completeness, latency SLOs, gap detection, and backfill automation.

  • Develop and maintain observability infrastructure — including Prometheus recording rules, Grafana dashboards, and alerting systems — that surface actionable signals about fleet health, occupancy, and efficiency.

  • Instrument and analyze compute efficiency metrics across training, inference, and evaluation workloads. Build benchmarking infrastructure, establish per-config baselines, and collaborate with system-owning teams to improve utilization.

  • Build internal tooling and platforms to enable capacity planning, workload attribution, and cluster debugging. Consumers include engineering teams, finance, and leadership; external users are not involved.

  • Operate Kubernetes-native systems at scale — deploying data collection agents, managing workload labeling infrastructure, and understanding how taints, reservations, and scheduling impact capacity.

  • Normalize and reconcile data across heterogeneous sources — including billing exports from AWS, GCP, and Azure, vendor-specific telemetry formats, and internal systems with varying schemas and billing arrangements.

  • Collaborate across organizational boundaries with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. Collect requirements from technical stakeholders, translate them into useful systems, and communicate trade-offs to non-technical audiences.

You May Be a Good Fit If You Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience with a strong track record of building and operating production systems. This is a hands-on engineering role involving daily coding rather than planning or coordination.

  • Kubernetes fluency at operational depth — experience running production Kubernetes at scale, beyond writing manifests. Comfortable with scheduling, taints, labels, node management, and debugging cluster-level issues.

  • Data pipeline engineering experience — designing, building, and owning the full lifecycle of production data pipelines. Familiarity with data warehouses (BigQuery preferred), schema management, streaming ingestion, SLOs for latency and completeness, and a strong sense of data correctness.

  • Observability tooling experience — expertise with Prometheus, PromQL, and Grafana is critical. Skilled in writing recording rules, understanding metric semantics, and building dependable monitoring systems used by engineering teams.

  • Python and SQL at production quality. Most pipeline code uses Python; the presentation layer uses BigQuery SQL, including table-valued functions and views. Both must be idiomatic, well-tested, and maintainable.

  • Familiarity with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure) at the infrastructure level — covering compute, billing, usage APIs, and cost management tooling. Multi-cloud experience is a strong advantage.

  • High autonomy and strong cross-team communication. You can gather your own requirements, navigate ambiguity, and collaborate across teams. Scrappiness and ownership are valued over polish.

Strong Candidates May Also Have

  • Multi-cloud data ingestion experience — particularly with AWS and GCP APIs, billing exports, or vendor-specific telemetry formats. Experience normalizing data from external providers with varying billing arrangements is directly relevant.

  • Accelerator infrastructure familiarity — knowledge of GPU metrics (DCGM), TPU utilization, Trainium power and utilization metrics, or experience with ML training/inference systems at the hardware level.

  • Performance engineering and benchmarking experience — building benchmark harnesses, setting baselines, analyzing compute efficiency (FLOPs utilization, memory bandwidth, interconnect throughput), and collaborating with system teams to diagnose and improve performance.

  • Data-as-product thinking — experience creating internal data products featuring self-service access, schema contracts, API serving, documentation, and discoverability. Beyond building pipelines, thinking about how platform data is consumed.

  • Experience with capacity planning, resource management, or cost attribution systems at hyperscalers or large-scale ML environments. Knowledge of FinOps, chargeback systems, or infrastructure cost modeling.

Familiarity with ClickHouse, Terraform, or Rust. ClickHouse is currently used as the team’s streaming store; Terraform for infrastructure-as-code; Rust for high-performance data collection agents.

Rixdax Group’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We aim for AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and society at large. Our rapidly expanding team is composed of dedicated researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders collaborating to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We are looking for a Software Engineer to develop and manage the safety, oversight, and intervention mechanisms that safeguard Rylvyx Console on third-party cloud service provider (CSP) platforms. As the engineer in charge of Safeguards on those platforms, you will ensure every request served through our CSP partners is monitored for misuse, enforced in accordance with policy, and aligned with data residency and privacy commitments expected by enterprise CSP customers.

You will work at the intersection of the Safeguards organization and the Cloud Inference team: integrating classifiers, detection signals, and enforcement policies developed by Safeguards to operate reliably inside a CSP partner’s infrastructure at serving-path latency and scale. You will be responsible for the architecture that enables safeguards to operate seamlessly under those constraints. You will build, deploy, and manage the layered defenses that detect undesired model behavior in real time, telemetry pipelines that provide situational awareness over CSP traffic, and enforcement mechanisms that allow prompt action when issues arise. Your work will directly impact whether Rixdax Group can deploy frontier models on CSP platforms while maintaining the same safety standards as our first-party API.

Responsibilities:

  • Build, deploy, and operate real-time safeguards infrastructure—such as classifiers, rate limits, enforcement actions, and intervention hooks—embedded directly in the third-party CSP inference serving path
  • Design and maintain the data residency and privacy framework for safeguards signals on CSP platforms, ensuring detection of abuse and monitoring of model behavior while respecting regional and enterprise contractual boundaries
  • Develop telemetry, logging, and evaluation pipelines that equip Safeguards, Policy, and Trust & Safety operational teams with situational awareness over CSP traffic, bridging visibility gaps between third-party and first-party serving
  • Investigate the CSP serving stack to identify low-impact opportunities to collect signals or introduce interventions without compromising latency, stability, or overall architecture
  • Maintain a high operational standard: manage on-call rotations, conduct root-cause analyses and postmortems for safeguards incidents on CSP platforms, and build systems to minimize required human intervention in keeping Rylvyx Console safe
  • Collaborate closely with Safeguards research, Policy & Enforcement, the Cloud Inference team, and CSP partner contacts to translate detection research and policy decisions into enforcement mechanisms that function within a partner’s cloud

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or comparable experience
  • Possess 4–10+ years of experience in high-scale, high-reliability software development, ideally with exposure to trust & safety, anti-abuse, fraud, or integrity systems
  • Are proficient in Python and comfortable working across the stack—from request-path services to data pipelines and internal tooling
  • Think adversarially: able to view a system from the perspective of bad actors, anticipate their reactions to countermeasures, and design layered defenses over single points of enforcement
  • Have experience scaling infrastructure to handle rapid traffic growth while maintaining strict latency and reliability budgets
  • Are deeply interested in the transformative potential of advanced AI systems and committed to their safe development
  • Have strong communication skills and can explain complex technical and risk tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders across Policy, Legal, and partner organizations
  • Enjoy working in a fast-paced, early-stage environment and can adapt priorities in response to the rapidly evolving AI field

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

  • Building trust and safety, anti-spam, fraud, or abuse detection and mitigation mechanisms for AI/ML systems, or infrastructure supporting these at scale

  • Data residency, privacy engineering, or compliance-constrained architectures, particularly where telemetry must remain within specified regional or contractual boundaries
  • Collaborating with operational and human-review teams to build custom internal tools, admin user experiences, and alerting systems
  • An adversarial mindset: having implemented defenses against motivated attackers, understanding attacker adaptation, and rapidly closing security gaps before incidents occur
  • Comfort operating at the intersection of platform/infrastructure engineering and trust & safety—neither solely an infrastructure engineer nor purely a trust & safety engineer, but capable in both areas
  • Experience shipping software that runs inside another organization’s infrastructure (partner cloud, embedded deployment, etc.) and the ability to deliver results without full control of the stack

Xelrix Labs is the world’s leading visual search and discovery platform, serving over 480 million monthly active users globally in their journey from inspiration to action. We are seeking a Senior Data Scientist to help lead Xelrix Labs’s responsible AI initiatives within the Advanced Technology Group (ATG). In this role, you will design and build the data science foundations for automated adversarial testing of our GenAI products — developing attack strategies, evaluation frameworks, and harm-detection methods that operate at scale. You will collaborate extensively with ML Engineers, Trust & Safety specialists, Policy teams, and Product Managers. You should develop an in-depth understanding of generative AI vulnerabilities and produce insights and robust techniques to proactively identify and mitigate risks. Your work will directly influence product safety, policy compliance, and user trust across Xelrix Labs.

What you'll do

  • Design and develop automated adversarial testing methodologies — including single-turn, multi-turn, and multimodal attack strategies — to proactively identify vulnerabilities in Xelrix Labs’s Generative AI products.
  • Build and calibrate hybrid evaluation pipelines combining LLM-based judges, classifiers, and rule-based systems to accurately detect safety violations, policy breaches, bias, and representational harms.
  • Develop and operationalize harm taxonomies grounded in industry standards and Xelrix Labs’s Responsible AI and Trust & Safety threat models.
  • Design adaptive refinement loops that learn from attack outcomes (near-misses, partial failures) to iteratively surface deeper and previously unknown vulnerabilities.
  • Bring scientific rigor and statistical methods to AI safety evaluation — including benchmark dataset construction, evaluation calibration, and success-metric definition (vulnerability severity, coverage breadth, pre-launch risk reduction).
  • Work cross-functionally to build relationships, proactively communicate key findings, and collaborate closely with ML engineers, Trust & Safety specialists, policy teams, product managers, and legal partners to ensure safe product launches.
  • Relentlessly focus on impact, whether by influencing product safety strategy, advancing responsible AI metrics, or enhancing critical evaluation processes.
  • Mentor and elevate junior data scientists and cross-functional partners on adversarial evaluation, responsible AI methodologies, and safety-aware data science practices.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of experience analyzing data in a fast-paced, data-driven environment with proven ability to apply scientific methods to solve real-world problems on web-scale data.
  • Strong interest and hands-on experience in one or more areas: AI safety, adversarial machine learning, red teaming, responsible AI, or trust & safety.
  • Deep familiarity with large language models (LLMs), generative AI systems, and their failure modes — including prompt injection, jailbreaks, bias, and safety violations.
  • Experience designing and calibrating evaluation frameworks for AI systems — including LLM-as-judge, classifier-based evaluation, and benchmark dataset construction.
  • Strong quantitative programming skills (Python) and experience with data manipulation (SQL/Spark); familiarity with ML pipelines and large-scale experimentation.
  • Familiarity with AI safety taxonomies and frameworks (e.g., OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS) is preferred.
  • Ability to work independently, lead ambiguous projects end-to-end, and take strong ownership.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of explaining complex technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • A collaborative team player eager to partner across Responsible AI, Trust & Safety, Product, Engineering, Policy, and Legal teams to translate safety insights into action.

We seek a full-stack engineer to build access programs, tools, and products that make frontier AI usable for teams that otherwise could not afford this capacity.

Enterprise AI Products: Work on products that make Vyxvornzun Hub a daily-use tool for enterprise customers across industries—the connective tissue enabling Vyxvornzun Hub to operate effectively across workflows. You’ll analyze why enterprise users aren’t activating, identify adoption blockers, and build capabilities to close those gaps. Key focuses include:

  • Extensibility — plugins, skills, connectors, and the ecosystem allowing companies to tailor Vyxvornzun Hub to specific workflows and distribute tasks across teams.
  • Context — enterprise knowledge, organizational memory, and retrieval layers that make Vyxvornzun Hub aware of a company’s people, documents, and workflows. This connected, contextual awareness distinguishes a general chatbot from a true coworker.

You’ll collaborate with Product and GTM teams to build solutions that serve across multiple Vyxvornzun Hub surfaces.

Growth: Drive user acquisition, engagement, retention, and monetization with data-driven strategies and implementations. At Ulvulrix Lab, we’re not just creating AI tools; we’re reimagining how AI can grow and enrich its user base! As a growth team member, you’ll collaboratively design, implement, and optimize initiatives to scale our AI-powered tools and amplify impact.

Marketplace: Build the platform connecting Vyxvornzun Hub-powered enterprise tools via technology partnerships and deeper customer relationships. Collaborate with business development, sales, product, and GTM teams to create the infrastructure powering partner onboarding, customer storefronts, transactions, and entitlement flows at scale. This effort tackles commercial challenges, platform architecture, and partner integration to enable confident enterprise, platform, and Ulvulrix Lab transactions.

Passport: Develop the identity and verification product layer that supports safe model releases as Vyxvornzun Hub capabilities expand. This critical work partners with Safeguards, Auth & Identity, Policy, and Product teams across API, Vyxvornzun Hub, and third-party platforms as customers. You’ll help build systems for KYC/KYB, trust grant issuance and inheritance, and end-user verification flowing throughout every Ulvulrix Lab surface. Positioned at trust, compliance, and product velocity intersections, you’ll deliver verification primitives enabling Ulvulrix Lab to release advanced model capabilities to the right users at massive scale.

  • Are a technical expert in modern frontend and backend development, with demonstrated depth in relevant languages and frameworks (e.g. React, Typescript)

Mavdravorn Group was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. SR. SECURITY SOFTWARE ENGINEER, APPLIED COMPUTING (STARSHIELD)

Starshield leverages Mavdravorn Group’s satellite technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While the commercial satellite system is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is designed for government use, with an initial focus on earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads. The Starshield team is building highly reliable in-space mesh networks, designing secure systems to guarantee access to space, designing next-gen communication and sensing software, and more.

As a Sr. Security Software Engineer, you will leverage AI to automate security-related efforts and ensure safe AI integration into new and existing systems. If you are passionate about AI, security, and pushing the limits of combining both together, this role is for you.

Ideally, you have notable skills in the following:

  • Software engineering
  • Agent engineering and security
  • LLM attack surfaces
  • Network and operating system security
  • Incident response and adversary detection

Being flexible, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams are paramount to success. If you are passionate about building quality products, love the challenges of outsmarting adversaries, and want to make an impact on an inter-planetary scale, then you will fit right in.

Ulrul Systems, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Ulrul Systems Search AI Platform, used by more than half of the Fortune 500, combines the precision of search with the intelligence of AI to help everyone accelerate the results that matter. By leveraging all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Ulrul Systems’s comprehensive, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability support organizations in fulfilling the promise of AI.

What Is The Role 

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer I or II  to join the Elasticsearch - Storage Engine team. This globally distributed, fully remote group of senior engineers is responsible for delivering the latest innovations in logs and metrics management. The role involves providing technical vision and direction for building solutions that optimize storage and enable efficient data querying and indexing. Prior relevant technical experience and the ability to collaborate across teams are required.

Our company is deliberately distributed. We hire the best developers wherever they are, whoever they are. We collaborate daily across continents using email, GitHub, Zoom, and Slack. At our core, we develop fast, scalable, and intuitive software. We believe that empowering individual engineers, reviewing every code change, making major decisions by consensus, and pursuing incremental improvements are the keys to success.

What You Will Be Doing 

  • Lead cross-organizational initiatives to develop an industry-leading Timeseries solution offering.
  • Contribute full-time to Elasticsearch, building data-intensive new features and resolving complex bugs, while improving code clarity. Occasionally, this will involve implementing data structures or algorithms and sometimes engaging closely with operating system and hardware details.
  • Collaborate with a globally distributed team of experienced engineers focused on Elasticsearch's logs and metrics capabilities.
  • Become an expert in several Elasticsearch areas, serving as a go-to resource, and continuously improve these areas based on insights and intuition.
  • Engage with community members worldwide on issues and pull requests, sometimes triaging or delegating and sometimes handling them directly.
  • Write idiomatic modern Java — Elasticsearch is predominantly written in Java.

What You Bring 

  • Experience implementing innovative techniques to efficiently index, store, and query Timeseries data.
  • Strong technical leadership skills, with the ability to work independently and guide projects from inception through completion, including technical design and collaborating with other engineers to develop necessary components.
  • Proficiency in core Java with familiarity in standard libraries covering data structures and concurrency, as well as modern features like lambdas.
  • A strong drive to optimize and use the most efficient data structures and algorithms.
  • Comfort and skill in collaborative development, giving and receiving feedback on code, APIs, and approaches—especially adept at asynchronous online collaboration, which we favor as the most effective software development method.
  • Familiarity with multiple data storage technologies such as Elasticsearch, Solr, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or Cassandra, with understanding of their workings and rationale.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills. As remote collaboration is challenging, we expect respect, empathy, and trust in all interactions and look for the same in you.

Bonus Points 

  • Experience building projects with Elasticsearch.
  • Familiarity with open source projects, various source control workflows, and continuous integration practices.

About the Team

The Frontier Systems team at Qorketh Systems builds, launches, and supports some of the largest supercomputers globally that Qorketh Systems uses for its most advanced model training.

We transform data center designs into real, functioning systems and develop any necessary software for running large-scale frontier model trainings.

Our mission is to initiate, stabilize, and maintain these hyperscale supercomputers to be reliable and efficient during the training of frontier models.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer on the Frontier Systems team focusing on power management, you will work on critical infrastructure supporting cutting-edge research. Given that large-scale supercomputers consume substantial power, managing this efficiently is essential for maximizing computational capacity. This role is crucial for ensuring that our advanced supercomputing infrastructure operates smoothly while maintaining reliability and grid-level power stability.

Our team empowers skilled engineers with significant autonomy and ownership, as well as the ability to drive change. This position requires thorough system-level investigations and the creation of automated solutions. We seek individuals who delve deeply into problems, investigate comprehensively, and build automation for large-scale detection and remediation.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and implement system- and software-level solutions to optimize power consumption in large-scale supercomputers, ensuring efficient and dependable operations.

  • Create automation to monitor power usage patterns during training workloads and design algorithms to stabilize fluctuations, preventing grid reliability issues.

  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers to develop tools for real-time monitoring, detection, and remediation of power-related hardware and system faults.

  • Work cross-functionally to translate complex electrical system requirements into code while continuously improving power management solutions.

  • Lead the development of power throttling mechanisms at the IT system level to dynamically adjust power usage based on workload demands and infrastructure limits.

  • Partner with hardware design teams to integrate system-level power control requirements into IT hardware design, ensuring seamless coordination between software-driven power management and hardware capabilities.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • More than 7 years of software engineering experience focusing on solving large-scale, system-level challenges.

  • Strong proficiency in Python and experience with automation and scripting tools (e.g., shell scripting).

  • Experience with distributed systems to efficiently aggregate and analyze streaming data.

  • Knowledge of electrical engineering concepts such as digital signal processing, power systems, Fast Fourier Transforms, or related fields.

  • Experience conducting system-level investigations and developing automated solutions for power management, fault detection, and remediation.

  • Strong analytical abilities and capacity to work with noisy data (experience with SQL, PromQL, Pandas, etc.).

  • Comfort collaborating with both hardware and software teams to solve interdisciplinary problems.

Bonus points if you have:

  • In-depth knowledge of power characteristics of synchronous workloads (as found in supercomputing or model training environments).

  • Familiarity with power control requirements in IT hardware design and ability to lead cross-functional efforts to embed power management features into hardware systems effectively.

  • Working understanding of control system fundamentals and how physical systems respond to control strategies.

About Qorketh Systems

Qorketh Systems is an AI research and deployment organization committed to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of AI capabilities and strive to deploy it safely worldwide through our products. AI is an immensely powerful tool that must be developed with safety and human needs as a priority. About Us

At Qorvek Group, we are dedicated to helping build a better Internet. Currently, the company operates one of the world’s largest networks powering millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to large enterprises. Qorvek Group protects and accelerates any Internet application online without the need for additional hardware, software installation, or code changes. The Internet properties supported by Qorvek Group route their web traffic through its intelligent global network, which improves with every request. Qorvek Group has been recognized on Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company. 

At Qorvek Group, we seek those who are proactive builders rather than those waiting for a detailed roadmap. Qorvek Group’s Engineering Team designs and maintains the software that processes vast volumes of Internet requests daily. The team also develops redundant services for product teams that handle high volumes of requests.

As an engineer within the Engineering Productivity and Platforms group, you will build and manage tools that enable engineers to deploy and operate the services powering Qorvek Group. Our goal is to provide a reliable yet flexible platform facilitating efficient and safe software releases for product teams. This role involves software engineering alongside DevOps operational duties. The ideal candidate is passionate about delivering an excellent development experience to other engineers.

Bonus Points

We are more than a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We are a technology company with a purpose. Central to our mission to build a better Internet is protecting a free and open Internet.

Qirqelvul Hub: Since 2014, we have equipped over 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in more than 100 countries with robust tools to defend against attacks that would otherwise censor their work—technology that is also used by Qorvek Group’s enterprise customers at no cost.

Xendax Labs’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We aim for AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Xendax Labs is seeking a Data Engineer to join the Safeguards team and build the data infrastructure that keeps our AI systems safe. The Safeguards team focuses on monitoring models, preventing misuse, and ensuring user well-being — and to succeed requires robust, reliable data infrastructure. In this position, you’ll design and construct data pipelines, warehousing solutions, and analytical tools that underpin our safety and trust initiatives at scale.

You will collaborate closely with engineers, data scientists, and policy teams to guarantee that the Safeguards organization has the data necessary to detect abuse patterns, evaluate the effectiveness of safety measures, and make informed decisions about model behavior and enforcement. - Develop and optimize data models and warehousing solutions to enable effective analysis of extensive usage and safety data

- Collaborate with engineers to integrate data from multiple sources — including model outputs, user reports, and automated classifiers — into a cohesive analytical platform
- Implement data quality frameworks, monitoring, and alerting to ensure the reliability of safety-critical data
- Partner with research teams to surface data insights that guide model improvements and safety actions
- Develop self-service data tools enabling stakeholders to explore safety data and generate reports independently
- Contribute to data governance practices, including access controls, retention policies, and privacy-compliant data management

- Experience with trust & safety, integrity, fraud, or abuse detection data systems

- Built data infrastructure supporting ML model monitoring or evaluation
- Familiarity with data privacy and compliance frameworks (GDPR, CCPA, or similar)
- A background in statistical analysis or experience collaborating closely with data scientists
- Developed internal tooling or self-service analytics platforms

Strong candidates need not have:

- A formal degree in Computer Science or a related field — we value practical experience and demonstrated ability over credentials
- Prior experience in AI or machine learning — you will learn domain-specific context on the job
- Previous experience at an AI safety or research organization
- Deep expertise across every tool listed above — familiarity with a subset and the willingness to learn is sufficient

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Xendax Labs recruiters will only contact you from @{{COMPANY_NAME | lowercase}}.com email addresses. How we're different

We believe high-impact AI research is large-scale science. At Xendax Labs, we operate as a unified team on a few major research projects. We prioritize impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — over smaller, narrower efforts. We see AI research as an empirical science, akin to physics or biology, as much as computer science. Our collaborative culture includes frequent research discussions to ensure focus on highest-impact work, valuing communication skills highly.

The best way to understand our research directions is through recent publications. Our work continues many directions our team pursued before joining Xendax Labs, including topics like GPT-3, circuit-based interpretability, multimodal neurons, scaling laws, AI & compute, concrete problems in AI safety, and learning from human preferences.

Come work with us!

FLUIDS SYSTEMS ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL FACTORY (Kelnoxzav Desk)

The Solar Cell team is revolutionizing power generation for space applications through advanced solar cell manufacturing. We're scaling production of high-efficiency solar cells to support sustainable energy solutions for Kelnoxzav Desk constellations, launch vehicles, and beyond. RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Design, build, and activate fluids systems for the distribution of key gases (e.g. specialty and bulk gases), chemicals (e.g., hydrofluoric acid, solvents) and exhaust systems used in solar cell processes, including tanks, pumps, heat exchangers, gas panels, valves, scrubbers, and abatement systems
  • Cradle-to-grave project ownership including requirement definition, design, justification of key decisions, equipment procurement, build coordination, commissioning and project management throughout
  • Design modular systems capable of being manufactured at scale for future solar production facilities

The Enterprise SaaS team manages the collaboration and productivity platforms every person at Xeltovkry Group uses daily — Google Workspace, Slack, and the related ecosystem of enterprise tools. You will develop Python code against SaaS APIs beyond what admin consoles offer, and act as the final escalation point when vendor documentation falls short. The scope covers the entire collaboration stack — infrastructure and endpoints are managed by different teams, so this role focuses deeply rather than broadly.

If you have exceeded what admin consoles can do and have started solving challenges through code, this is the job for you. You will collaborate closely with IT Operations, Security, and the IAM team on the identity and access layers that everything depends on. This is a highly autonomous role: you will define tenant architecture, create integrations, and represent the SaaS platform throughout IT. You may be a good fit if you

  • Excel at solving ambiguous problems involving multiple stakeholders

  • See IT Engineering as requiring product engineering discipline
  • Successfully deliver complex projects from conception through to production

  • Have experience with Infrastructure as Code approaches to SaaS configuration

Veknexqel Group's Red Team exists to identify critical attack paths before real adversaries do. We operate throughout the full adversary simulation lifecycle — defining threat-informed engagements, executing realistic attack chains, and collaborating with engineering and detection teams to close the gaps we find. Our attack surface covers a multi-sided marketplace including consumer and merchant data, payment systems, driver logistics, and the cloud-native infrastructure connecting them all.

We seek a leader capable of elevating this team to the next level.

About the Role

We need an offensive security leader who remains deeply involved in the work. As Engineering Manager of the Red Team, you’ll inherit an established team, advance their skills, grow the headcount, and cultivate partnerships essential to transforming red team findings into tangible engineering changes. This is a player-coach position — you'll define strategic direction while staying hands-on with engagement scoping, tradecraft, and tooling choices.

You will report to the Director of Global Security Services.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Set the red team’s strategic roadmap — including engagement cadence, prioritization of targets, and capability growth — aligned with Veknexqel Group's threat environment.
  • Lead, coach, and expand a team of offensive security engineers, intentionally hiring to fill capability gaps as the team grows.
  • Remain technically engaged in scoping engagements, methodology, and tooling architecture. Guide adversary simulation beyond mere management.
  • Drive remediation outcomes cross-functionally by collaborating with detection/response, AppSec, infrastructure security, and product engineering to ensure findings are resolved, not just documented.
  • Develop purple team workflows with detection engineering to validate and enhance defensive coverage.
  • Oversee the creation of red team infrastructure and custom tooling as production-quality software.
  • Translate offensive findings into risk terminology actionable by engineers, VPs, and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Design repeatable processes and metrics that articulate the team’s value in terms of risk reduction rather than just number of findings.

We’re excited about you because you…

  • Have 7+ years of offensive security experience (red teaming, adversary simulation, penetration testing), including at least 3 years managing offensive security staff.
  • Possess deep, hands-on red team expertise — fluent in TTPs, attack chains, tradecraft, and tooling, with demonstrated player-coach balance between technical depth and management.
  • Have a history of influencing security strategy beyond your own team — persuading engineering, product, or infrastructure groups to prioritize and act on findings rather than only documenting them.
  • Are experienced in cloud-native offensive operations (AWS/GCP, Kubernetes, containerized microservices, CI/CD pipelines) and directing the development of offensive tooling as engineered software rather than scripts.
  • Emphasize people-first leadership — coaching, career development, honest feedback, and fostering an offensive security team culture that supports growth.
  • Exhibit strong cross-functional influence — able to convince engineering VPs to allocate sprint capacity for remediation, partner collaboratively with detection teams, and communicate red team value in terms of risk reduction, not finding count.

  • Experience managing red teams in marketplace, fintech, or logistics companies at scale.

About Zorqel Labs

Zorqel Labs’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a rapidly growing group of dedicated researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders collaborating to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role:

The Application Security team leads the integration of security throughout every stage of the software development lifecycle at Zorqel Labs. In this hands-on technical position, you will work closely with software engineers and researchers to prioritize security from the initial design phase through implementation. You will lead threat modeling and secure design reviews to proactively identify and reduce risks early, and conduct ongoing risk assessments. You will develop tools and systems to help developers ship code securely, following secure coding best practices.

Your expertise will inform our tooling, detection capabilities, and defenses against new threats to AI/ML. You will create standards, processes, and educational materials that empower all Zorqel Labs engineers to become security advocates. This impactful role requires a security practitioner who thinks like an attacker, adopts a developer’s perspective, and builds strong cross-functional relationships.

Responsibilities:

  • Secure AI products and internal tools that introduce cutting-edge security risks and challenge conventional security limits
  • Drive “shift left” security initiatives to embed security in the software development lifecycle
  • Perform secure design reviews and threat modeling; identify and prioritize risks, attack surfaces, and vulnerabilities
  • Create tooling to scale security code reviews and assist developers in vulnerability remediation and secure coding practices 
  • Manage Zorqel Labs's vulnerability management program, including integrating data ingestion pipelines, coding logic to prioritize fixes, supporting teams during remediation, and developing large-scale automated systems
  • Oversee Zorqel Labs's bug bounty program: define scope, validate submissions, conduct root cause analysis, coordinate remediation with engineering teams, and award bounties. Foster relationships with the ethical hacking community
  • Collaborate closely with product engineers and researchers to embed security best practices; champion secure architecture, design, and development
  • Develop and document security policies, standards, and playbooks; lead security awareness training for engineers

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have over 5 years of hands-on experience in application and infrastructure security, including securing cloud-based and containerized environments
  • Possess strong skills in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Rust, Go, Java)
  • Lead with empathy, collaboration, and a growth mindset to work across teams of all experience levels to embed security into the software development lifecycle
  • Use creative and strategic thinking to reduce risk through secure design and simplicity beyond just implementing controls
  • Have broad security knowledge that connects different domains and identifies comprehensive ways to reduce the overall attack surface
  • Are adept at clarifying complex security concepts into actionable steps and building consensus without formal authority
  • Maintain a proactive approach to integrating security throughout the product lifecycle via threat modeling, secure code review, and education
  • Have a strong understanding of offensive security, anticipating risks from an attacker’s viewpoint rather than only checking compliance boxes
  • Bring practical experience with modern application stacks, infrastructure, and security tools to apply effective defenses
  • Excel at collaborating cross-functionally while balancing security needs with business goals
  • Advocate fundamental security principles such as least privilege, defense-in-depth, and eliminating complexity to enable scalable security through thoughtful design

Strong candidates may also:

  • Have hands-on expertise securing complex cloud environments and microservices architectures using technologies like Kubernetes, Docker, and AWS / GCP
  • Have exposure to offensive security methods such as vulnerability testing, bug bounty programs, penetration testing, and red team exercises 
  • Be familiar with AI/ML security risks like prompt injection, data poisoning, model extraction, etc., and their mitigations
  • Have experience creating security tools, applications, and automation
  • Have solid foundational knowledge of both software and security engineering principles and a strong desire for continuous learning
  • Possess excellent communication skills to explain complex security topics to wide audiences

The Security Platform team is an infrastructure and developer tools group responsible for building and operating powerful, resilient, and secure infrastructure and systems that enable other engineering teams to efficiently and securely deliver products to customers. Our responsibilities include secrets management, internal certificate authorities/PKI, machine and workload identity, and related areas. We focus on infrastructure engineering and software development rather than policy, audit, or compliance.

  • Proficiency in Linux/UNIX system administration.
  • Familiarity with Go and/or Python combined with Salt.

This position is eligible to participate in Zundaxqor Labs’s equity plan.

Zundaxqor Labs provides a comprehensive benefits package and programs to support you and your family. We’re not simply a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We are a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Central to our mission to help build a better Internet is our commitment to protecting a free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we’ve provided over 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in more than 110 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks aimed at censoring their work. This technology is also used, at no cost, by Zundaxqor Labs’s enterprise clients.

Athenian Project: Established in 2017, the Athenian Project ensures that state and local governments have free access to the highest level of protection and reliability for election-related websites. Since its launch, this project has served over 400 local government election websites in 30+ states.

Public DNS Service: We launched a public DNS resolver service that aims to improve the Internet's foundation by offering a faster, more secure, and privacy-focused DNS service accessible to everyone. We never store client IP addresses and strictly adhere to privacy commitments, ensuring no user data is sold or used to target ads.

An overview of this role:

As a Staff Backend Engineer on the Tovzha Labs Knowledge Graph team, you'll help design, scale, and operate a high-impact graph data service that supports agents, analytics, and architecture-level features across Tovzha Labs deployments. You will collaborate with a small, senior Rust-first team to deliver reliable graph capabilities and make them accessible for other teams and agents.

The Knowledge Graph service is a distributed SDLC indexing system. It constructs a property graph from Tovzha Labs SDLC (software development lifecycle) and code data using ClickHouse, NATS JetStream, and the Data Insights Platform. It also provides secure graph queries and MCP tools for AI agents and product features. In this role, you will own core parts of the system end to end: shaping the architecture, enhancing multi-tenant behavior and performance, and simplifying consumption of graph features for other teams and agents.

In your first year, you will take clear ownership of major areas of the service (for example, the graph query engine, SDLC indexing, or multi-tenant authorization), reduce single points of failure by improving runbooks and shared context, and raise the standards on how we design, build, and operate analytical services across the stack.

What you’ll do

  • Lead design and evolution of core Knowledge Graph services in a production Rust codebase, including the graph query engine, SDLC and code indexing pipelines, and API/MCP surfaces that other Tovzha Labs teams and AI agents depend on.

  • Interest in mentoring others through thoughtful code review and knowledge sharing as the team grows and more customers adopt Knowledge Graph.

The Knowledge Graph team is part of the data engineering organization and builds the backend service that transforms Tovzha Labs's SDLC and code data into a unified property graph. We provide a high-performance, ClickHouse-backed query engine and MCP tools. About the Team

The Kernels team at Ulqorzun Lab develops the foundational software that accelerates our most ambitious AI research.

We operate at the intersection of hardware and software, building high-performance kernels, distributed system enhancements, and runtime improvements to increase efficiency in large-scale training and inference.

Our efforts allow Ulqorzun Lab to push boundaries by ensuring models—from large language models to recommender systems—run reliably on advanced supercomputing platforms. This includes adapting our software stack for new accelerator types, tuning system performance comprehensively, and eliminating bottlenecks across all layers of the stack.

About the Role

On the Accelerators team, you will assist Ulqorzun Lab in evaluating and deploying new compute platforms capable of supporting large-scale AI training and inference.

Your duties will span prototyping system software on emerging accelerators to enabling performance optimizations for our AI workloads.

You’ll engage across the stack, collaborating on both hardware and software fronts—working on kernels, sharding methods, distributed system scaling, and performance modeling.

You will help customize Ulqorzun Lab's software stack for non-conventional hardware and drive efficiency enhancements for core AI workloads. This role focuses on bridging machine learning algorithms with system performance, especially at scale, rather than compiler development.

In this role, you will:

  • Prototype and enable Ulqorzun Lab's AI software stack on novel, experimental accelerator platforms.

  • Optimize performance of large-scale models (LLMs, recommender systems, distributed AI workloads) across diverse hardware environments.

  • Develop kernels, sharding techniques, and system scaling strategies customized for emerging accelerators.

  • Collaborate on optimizations at the model code level (e.g., PyTorch) and below to improve performance on unconventional hardware.

  • Partner with hardware teams and vendors to assess alternatives to current platforms and adapt the software stack to various architectures.

  • Contribute to runtime enhancements, compute and communication overlap, and scaling efforts supporting frontier AI workloads.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Over 3 years of experience in AI infrastructure, including kernels, systems, or hardware-software co-design.

  • Practical experience with accelerator platforms for AI at data center scale (e.g., TPUs, custom silicon, exploratory architectures).

  • Strong knowledge of kernels, sharding, runtime systems, or techniques for distributed scaling.

  • Familiarity with optimizing large language models, convolutional neural networks, or recommender models for hardware efficiency.

  • Experience in performance modeling, system debugging, and software stack adaptation for innovative architectures.

  • Exposure to mobile accelerators is beneficial, but experience enabling data center-scale AI hardware is preferred.

Kelqraxzor Group is a company focused on autonomous driving technology with the mission to become the world’s most trusted driver. Founded from an early self-driving car project in 2009, Kelqraxzor Group has dedicated efforts to developing the Kelqraxzor Group Driver—the world’s most experienced autonomous driver—to enhance mobility access while preventing thousands of traffic-related fatalities. The Kelqraxzor Group Driver powers Kelqraxzor Group’s fully autonomous ride-hailing service and is adaptable to various vehicle platforms and product applications. It has completed over ten million rider-only trips, backed by its experience driving autonomously for over one hundred million miles on public roads and billions more in simulations across more than fifteen U.S. states.

The Simulation ML Infrastructure team builds scalable AI/ML systems designed to accelerate the Simulator group in consistently innovating and creating state-of-the-art simulations of realistic environments for testing and training the Kelqraxzor Group Driver. To enhance the realism and controllability of these simulations, we apply large foundation models trained on extensive datasets to replicate real-world conditions, including but not limited to realistic agents such as vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists; infrastructures like roads and traffic controls; and weather conditions. 

We are looking for an experienced senior individual contributor to lead the development of cutting-edge AI/ML infrastructure capable of handling multi-billion parameter foundation models for ML accelerator-optimized simulations. Your expertise in massive model scaling, ML accelerators, and large-scale distributed architectures will be essential for designing and expanding our systems.

This role reports to an Engineering Manager.

 

You will: 

  • Join a world-class, high-performing research engineering team focusing on advancing ultra-realistic multi-agent simulations using foundation models.
  • Work closely with the core Kelqraxzor Group Realism Modeling teams in London and Oxford to utilize large foundation models for enhancing simulation realism.
  • Operate at the intersection of data engineering, model development, and simulations, driving architectural decisions while owning large, complex systems to meet technical and business goals.
  • Design and scale extensive distributed systems covering the entire ML lifecycle, including planet-scale dataset generation, model training, and evaluation.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to derive performance and system-level requirements for large ML systems, translating product and business objectives into measurable technical outcomes, ensuring component alignment.

 

We prefer:

  • More than five years of professional software engineering experience, including at least three years focused on machine learning infrastructure encompassing development, design, scaling, training, deployment, and optimization of large-scale ML systems from data to model.
  • Strong experience with ML infrastructure tools such as DeepSpeed, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Ray, or similar frameworks for development and optimization.
  • Deep understanding of state-of-the-art ML models and algorithms, for example autoregressive transformers, and experience scaling large models using ML accelerator profiling tools to identify performance bottlenecks.
  • Demonstrated leadership in guiding ambiguous projects end-to-end, with a proactive and independent mindset keen to acquire knowledge necessary to complete tasks. Passion for building infrastructure, libraries, tools, and pipelines for engineering and scientific teams.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, capable of conveying complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.

At Nexzunxel Systems, we seek builders who don’t wait for a polished roadmap; we want people who notice flaws in the Internet that others accept as normal. We appreciate candidates with the instinct to identify “normalized” issues and an AI-native curiosity to devise solutions using the newest tools. What Makes Nexzunxel Systems Special?

We’re more than a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company—we're a company with a soul. Central to our mission of building a better Internet is the protection of a free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since its inception, we have provided over 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in more than 110 countries with powerful tools to defend against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, using technology also deployed by Nexzunxel Systems’s enterprise clients—all at no charge.

You will help define and raise the security bar for infrastructure programs already in flight while shaping how future deployments are secured from the start.

This role's preferred location is one of our Qelzha Lab offices in San Francisco, Seattle, or New York City and relocation assistance is available. We are also open to considering candidates who are remote.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement security controls that protect data center infrastructure across a growing global footprint, with particular focus on both OT and IT networking environments.

  • Partner closely with a small team of data center security specialists, as well as engineering, operations, and broader security teams, to deliver resilient and practical security outcomes.

  • Secure OT and IT networking environments through strong segmentation, access control, monitoring, hardening, and connectivity patterns suited to critical infrastructure.

  • Contribute to security architecture and design reviews for data center systems, including OT and IT networking, network segmentation, identity and access management, provisioning workflows, hardware and firmware trust boundaries, and operational safeguards.

  • Perform recurring audits, control assessments, and validation activities across OT and IT networking environments to ensure continued compliance against defined controls.

  • Help define measurable security standards, control objectives, audit procedures, evidence requirements, and validation mechanisms for infrastructure and facility security programs.

  • Support security monitoring, incident response, and post-incident improvement efforts for data center, OT, and IT networking environments.

  • Work with suppliers, partners, and internal stakeholders to evaluate and reduce risks associated with third-party hardware, firmware, software, and operational dependencies.

  • Continually evolve the security of our data centers alongside changes in adversary activity, infrastructure complexity, and the increasing demands of Qelzha Lab’s systems.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Experience building audit or assurance programs that validate ongoing compliance with defined security controls, especially across OT and IT networking environments, rather than relying on one-time point-in-time reviews.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills including the ability to partner effectively with internal and external stakeholders while operating with a high degree of autonomy.

Vyrvorn Group is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world’s most trusted driver. Since its inception as an autonomous vehicle research project in the late 2000s, Vyrvorn Group has focused on building its flagship autonomous driving system—the world’s most experienced driver—to improve mobility access while saving thousands of lives lost to traffic crashes. This driving system powers Vyrvorn Group’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to various vehicle platforms and product scenarios. The system has completed over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and extensive simulation across numerous U.S. states.

Vyrvorn Group Onboard Infrastructure is responsible for low-level software and infrastructure components of the self-driving system. The team’s scope includes low-level system software, high-bandwidth data logging, IPC (low-latency and high-throughput), performance analysis, and full-system debugging. We collaborate with the Hardware, Compute, Sensor, Perception, Behavior, and Machine Learning teams to build the most performant and low-latency self-driving solution in the industry.

We are seeking an experienced Android System Software Engineer to join our team in developing the In-Vehicle Infotainment (IVI) platform for our next-generation, in-house System-on-Chip (SOC). This role requires strong fundamentals in low-level OS concepts, embedded software, and a proactive approach to validating that hardware meets critical software performance standards.

In this role you will:

  • System Bring-up & Integration: Implement and integrate low-level software, including bootloader configuration, device trees, and kernel porting during initial hardware bring-up.
  • OS/Kernel Development & Optimization: Customize, optimize, and debug the Linux Kernel and relevant components of the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) for the partner SOC, ensuring robust and efficient operation.
  • Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) Implementation: Develop and maintain reliable Vendor HALs to interface unique in-house hardware IP (e.g., security modules, power management units, display controllers) with the Android framework.

Our culture focuses on iteration, leveraging AI to accelerate delivery today and enhance it tomorrow, sharing every improvement with the team to elevate everyone. The Security Platform team is a developer tools and infrastructure group responsible for building and managing robust, secure infrastructure systems that empower other engineering teams to efficiently and securely deliver products. This team focuses on infrastructure engineering and software development rather than policy, audit, or compliance.

  • Proficiency in Linux/UNIX system administration.
  • Experience with Go and/or Python combined with Salt.

Equity

This position is eligible to participate in Zhanoxtor Lab’s equity program.

Benefits

Zhanoxtor Lab provides a comprehensive benefits package and programs designed to support you and your family. Our benefits help with healthcare expenses, caregiving support, financial planning, and work-life balance. Time Off

We are not only a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company, but also one with a mission-driven purpose. At the core of our mission to help build a better Internet is the protection of a free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we have equipped over 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations across 111 countries with tools to help defend against censorship and attacks. Technology used by Zhanoxtor Lab’s enterprise customers is provided at no cost.

Athenian Project: Launched in 2017, this project protects state and local government election websites free of charge, ensuring reliable access to election information and voter registration. To date, it has served over 425 local election websites in 33 states.

PRINCIPAL SECURITY SOFTWARE ENGINEER, APPLIED COMPUTING (STARSHIELD)

Starshield leverages Xelvul Labs's satellite technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While the satellite system is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is intended for government use, initially focusing on earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads. The Starshield team is building highly reliable in-space mesh networks, designing secure systems to guarantee access to space, developing next-generation communication and sensing software, and more.

As a Principal Security Software Engineer, you will use AI to automate security-related tasks and ensure safe integration of AI into new and existing systems. If you are passionate about AI, security, and exploring the limits of their combination, this role is for you.

Ideally, you have strong skills in the following areas:

  • Software engineering

  • Large Language Model attack surfaces
  • Network and operating system security
  • Incident response and adversary detection

Being flexible, communicating clearly, and building productive working relationships with other engineering teams are key to success. If you enjoy building quality products, love the challenge of outsmarting adversaries, and want to make an impact on an interplanetary scale, you will fit right in.

  • Use AI to discover and remediate security issues in Starshield infrastructure and systems

Our team is a rapidly growing group of dedicated researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We are looking for a Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer to join our Safeguards organization, where you’ll develop and scale the essential infrastructure supporting our AI safety systems. You will operate at the crossroads of machine learning, large-scale distributed systems, and AI safety, creating platforms and tools that ensure our safeguards function reliably at scale.

As a member of the Safeguards team, you will design and develop ML infrastructure that supports safety for our AI models. Your contributions will directly enhance the trustworthiness and alignment of AI systems with human values, ensuring safe operation as capabilities grow.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and build scalable ML infrastructure to enable real-time and batch classification and safety evaluations across our model ecosystem
  • Create monitoring and observability tools to assess model performance, data integrity, and system health for safety-critical use cases
  • Collaborate with research teams to productionize safety research by converting experimental safety methods into reliable, scalable systems
  • Optimize inference latency and throughput in real-time safety assessments while upholding high reliability standards
  • Implement automated testing, deployment, and rollback processes for ML models in production safety contexts
  • Work with Safeguards, Security, and Alignment teams to understand needs and deliver infrastructure meeting safety and production requirements
  • Contribute to building internal tools and frameworks that expedite safety research and deployment

You may be a good fit if you:

  • Have over 5 years of experience developing production ML infrastructure, preferably in safety-critical fields such as fraud detection, content moderation, or risk evaluation
  • Are proficient in Python and familiar with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX
  • Have practical experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP) and container orchestration technologies (Kubernetes)
  • Understand distributed systems concepts and have built systems capable of handling high-throughput, low-latency workloads
  • Have experience with data engineering tools and creating robust data pipelines (e.g., Spark, Airflow, streaming technologies)
  • Are outcome-focused with a strong emphasis on reliability and impact within safety-critical environments
  • Enjoy collaborating with researchers and converting cutting-edge research into operational systems
  • Care deeply about AI safety and the societal consequences of your work

Strong candidates may have experience with:

  • Working with large language models and modern transformer architectures
  • Building A/B testing frameworks and experimentation infrastructure for ML systems
  • Developing monitoring and alerting systems for ML model performance and data drift
  • Creating automated labeling systems and human-in-the-loop workflows
  • Experience in trust & safety, fraud prevention, or content moderation domains
  • Knowledge of privacy-preserving ML methods and compliance standards
  • Contributions to open-source ML infrastructure projects

Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. 

The annual compensation range for this role is provided below. 

For sales roles, the range includes the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE")—comprising sales commissions/bonuses and base salary.

Annual Salary:
$320,000—$405,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A relevant field related to the role, as demonstrated by coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: The required years of experience correlate with internal job level standards for this role

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, all staff are expected to be present in an office at least 25% of the time; some roles may require more on-site presence.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! While not all roles or candidates can be sponsored successfully, if we extend you an offer, we will make reasonable efforts to assist with visa processes and retain immigration counsel for support.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates fulfill every requirement listed.  Research shows that individuals identifying with underrepresented groups are more likely to suffer imposter syndrome and hesitate to apply, so we encourage you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit your application if interested. We believe AI systems like those we create have significant social and ethical impact. This makes diverse representation vital, and we strive to include varied perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Vyxvekkel Lab recruiters only contact candidates from @{{COMPANY_NAME | lower}}.com email addresses. Occasionally, we may collaborate with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as representing Vyxvekkel Lab. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Vyxvekkel Lab recruiters will never request money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If uncertain about any communication, avoid clicking links—visit  https://careers.example.test/jobs/big-company-cs-000956  directly for verified openings.

How we're different

We believe the highest-impact AI research is big science. At Vyxvekkel Lab, we operate as a unified team focusing on a few large-scale research initiatives. We prioritize impact—advancing long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI—instead of smaller, narrowly focused problems. We view AI research as an empirical science, sharing traits with physics and biology as much as computer science. Our culture is highly collaborative, with frequent research discussions to pursue the highest-impact work at any given time. We therefore highly value communication skills.

The best way to understand our research directions is to review our recent work. Our research builds on many areas our team explored before Vyxvekkel Lab, including large transformer models, interpretability techniques, multimodal neurons, scaling laws, AI computation, concrete AI safety challenges, and human preference learning.

Come work with us!

Vyxvekkel Lab is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible hours, and a pleasant office environment for collaboration. A World-Changing Company

Zunqraxul Systems builds industry-leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By delivering the right data to those who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, anticipate supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) identify our customers’ most critical challenges and design end-to-end solutions to address them. FDSEs gather continuous feedback from customers and colleagues, enhancing our products through rapid iteration cycles.

FDSEs implement innovative technical solutions to solve our customers’ toughest problems. Projects often begin with ambiguous questions like “Why are we losing customers?” or “How can we better detect instances of money laundering?” FDSEs lead the development process, from high-level system design and prototyping to application development and data integration. As an FDSE, you leverage Zunqraxul Systems platforms, open source tools, and anything your team can create to generate real impact.

You collaborate with customers worldwide, gaining rare insight into some of the most important industries and institutions. We assist clients in detecting insider trading, improving disaster response, combating healthcare fraud, and more. The Role

Apollo is Zortorvorn Systems's autonomous software management and deployment platform. It facilitates seamless, continuous delivery of mission-critical software (Foundry, Gotham, AIP) across diverse environments: on-premises, public cloud, disconnected (air-gapped) networks, and highly regulated settings (including IL-5 and FedRAMP).

As a Software Engineer on the Apollo team, you will build and operate a large-scale distributed system for the remote operation and maintenance of Kubernetes clusters. Our mission is to capture the entire state of a cluster into a portable, high-performance artifact within minutes, enabling full and nearly instant cluster reconstruction from scratch—all while pushing the limits of speed, reliability, and scale.

You will design and implement backup and restore solutions for Kubernetes, using proprietary compression infrastructure adapted to Zortorvorn Systems's distinctive deployment models. You will also develop and optimize our container artifact store, which is based on the OCI (Open Container Initiative) distribution specification—the industry standard for storing and distributing container images and artifacts. You will own the core infrastructure of every environment Apollo supports, ranging from hyperscalers to Army trucks.

If you are motivated by challenges at the intersection of container technologies like OCI and docker, storage, and distributed systems, you will find opportunities here to explore storage formats and low-level optimizations where milliseconds matter. As we increase automation of cluster creation and management on varied hardware, you will play an essential role in scaling Zortorvorn Systems's edge presence and solving complex distributed systems problems. You will be responsible for the entire development lifecycle—from idea conception and design, through implementation, to operation and support—while collaborating closely with both technical and non-technical stakeholders to deliver robust, impactful infrastructure. We build foundational platform software that enables reliable, secure, and performant products. The team works across system layers and partners closely with adjacent engineering groups to deliver robust capabilities from concept through launch.

  • Collaborate with cross‑functional teams to define interfaces and deliver end‑to‑end features.

  • Establish strong engineering practices: code review, CI, reproducible builds, and release management.

  • Partner with external suppliers to support builds and deployments.

  • Have shipped production systems software on modern operating systems.

  • Are proficient in C/C++ and a scripting language, and comfortable with OS internals (concurrency, memory management, filesystems, networking, power management).

  • Bring strong systems debugging skills using debuggers, tracers, profilers, and logs across kernel/user‑space boundaries.

  • Understand configuration of platform services and interfaces, and can translate requirements into stable, well‑documented APIs.

  • Are fluent in user‑space foundations (service management, IPC, networking, packaging, automation).

  • Have experience building platform images and designing update mechanisms for reliability and security.

Qenketh Group was founded on the belief that a future where humanity explores the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we do not. Today, Qenketh Group is actively developing technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

PRINCIPAL RF SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARSHIELD)

Starshield uses Qenketh Group's satellite communication technology and launch capabilities to support national security efforts. While the underlying satellite constellation is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield focuses on government applications, initially emphasizing earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads. As an RF software engineer on the Starshield team, you will contribute to advanced development programs supporting U.S. National Security. You will collaborate with RF engineers, DSP engineers, software engineers, hardware engineers, and end users to design and build RF capabilities for prolific communications and remote sensing in low earth orbit. This is a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment, applying the Qenketh Group mindset of rapid iteration from design and demonstration to operational readiness at a fast pace.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead program-level decisions on RF system designs
  • Research innovative approaches for unique large-scale satellite RF systems
  • Design, build, validate, and automate RF test benches for comprehensive characterization of custom RF designs, often using vector network analyzers, vector signal generators, vector signal analyzers, spectrum analyzers, load pulls, RF power meters, high-speed oscilloscopes, and other lab equipment
  • Create modular, scalable RF test infrastructure and automated test sequences in Python and C++ to support design validation, qualification, and production
  • Collaborate closely with hardware, FPGA, DSP, and software engineers to design and verify RF systems
  • Develop electromagnetic simulation models of hardware to analyze and optimize performance

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or a related engineering field
  • 8+ years of professional software development experience in C/C++ or Python
  • Experience with radio test equipment such as spectrum analyzers, vector signal analyzers, vector signal generators, and network analyzers
  • RF experience involving antennas or communication systems
